answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a refundable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. One person can still create a nebula of fake accounts, but each must lock real capital, and repeated abuse burns it; the cost grows with the attack’s scale. Audits should sample work across a glacier of activity and compare outcomes, so Sybils cannot cheaply pass by copying one another. A grove of colluding accounts may still evade detection, but escrow makes mass identities expensive rather than free.
